strengths: Novel geometric perspective on reasoning collapse as spectral degeneration into low-rank manifolds, with clear intuitive visualization
Convincing empirical evidence of effective rank decrease during failed reasoning chains across four diverse benchmarks (Figure 3)
Strong empirical results on mathematical reasoning: 62.4% average accuracy improvement and 113.7% sampling efficiency gains on difficult subsets
Thorough experimental documentation including ablation studies (Table 3) and robustness analysis across random seeds (Table 4)
Ablation results (Table 3) validate that geometric selection mechanism matters: SOE (70.59%) outperforms random probe injection (58.82%)
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: only 4B parameter models evaluated; larger models (70B+) unvalidated despite claims of model-agnosticism; evaluation restricted exclusively to mathematical benchmarks with no testing on code generation, logical reasoning, or other domains
Weak experimental comparisons: only baseline is Self-Consistency sampling; missing comparisons with other inference-time reasoning methods, tree search, or ensemble approaches
Post-hoc intervention design limits practical applicability: requires generating failed traces first, then re-generating with 2.60s latency overhead per step

Circular reasoning in theoretical motivation: effective rank used to diagnose problem and to solve it; if EffRank is incorrect diagnostic, entire causal mechanism fails; causal claims are correlational not causal

Theoretical rigor issues: Proposition 1 proof is tautological and doesn't rigorously establish why nonlinearities cannot restore dimensionality; Theorem 2 proof incomplete and informal; no justification for why different model architectures guarantee orthogonal projections

Ambiguous methodology: truncation point selection described as critical but specified vaguely; no ablation studies on key hyperparameters (N=8, L=8, k eigenvectors); manifold dimension k selection not discussed

Results reported only on 'difficult subset' (incorrect+>4000 tokens): somewhat artificial, cherry-picked failure cases; unclear what full-dataset performance looks like; requires specific weak student model (Gemma-3-4B) with no justification or ablation
Weak semantic sparsity argument (Appendix D.3): claim that 8-token injection provides no information because 8≪8192 tokens ignores that information can concentrate in small regions
Restricted applicability: requires open-weight models with hidden state access, precluding evaluation on proprietary models; computational overhead makes deployment impractical

strengths: Novel geometric perspective on reasoning collapse as low-rank bias manifold concentration, well-motivated by effective rank decay analysis and clearly illustrated
Substantial empirical improvements across multiple challenging benchmarks (62.4% on AIME 2024, 113.7% average, with consistent gains on AIME 2025, Olympiad Bench, Omni-Math)
Well-designed three-phase SOE framework with clear algorithmic contributions (greedy trace monitoring, micro-SVD selection, orthogonal latent stitching)

Comprehensive experimental validation including ablation studies (Table 8), cross-family generalization (Table 3), matched-control rank decay analysis (Table 5), and robustness across random seeds (Table 10)
Strong generalization across heterogeneous model architectures (Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemini) and parameter scales without retraining
Detailed reproducibility support: worked example (Appendix A), hyperparameter specifications, latency breakdown (Figure 6), and code availability
weaknesses: Theoretical justification relies on simplified linear attention models (Propositions 1-2) whose connection to actual transformer behavior is assumed but unvalidated; gap between theory and practice remains
Causal claim that geometric concentration causes reasoning failure is not rigorously established—alternative interpretations (geometric concentration as symptom rather than root cause) not ruled out
Strictly limited to white-box scenarios; inapplicable to closed-source LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude) that dominate practice, reducing real-world impact
Post-hoc intervention doesn't address underlying training/architectural causes; requires careful per-model calibration of three phases, reducing reproducibility and generalizability

Experimental design issues: (1) Difficult Subset filtering may introduce selection bias; (2) Pass@16 evaluation conflates sampling efficiency gains with actual reasoning improvement; (3) high-temperature baseline (T=0.7) not compared against greedy decoding
Computational overhead substantial (~3.6s per problem) and not fully transparent relative to baselines; 12.8% runtime overhead under vLLM but downstream deployment implications unclear
Limited comparison with alternative methods addressing reasoning collapse (prompt engineering, ensemble approaches, other test-time interventions); PRM baseline comparison minimal
All validated models are >40B parameters; behavior on smaller models and sensitivity to Teacher-Student similarity not explored
Statistical significance testing and confidence intervals absent from main results; robustness analysis limited to AIME 2025 for rank decay phenomenon
Why orthogonal probes specifically outperform other geometric perturbations is under-explained; degree to which gains arise from injected information vs. geometric intervention mechanism unclear
